$source.HIG: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback (no change log on the page; captured 2026-09-28)
$source.WCAG: W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 (1.4.1 use of colour, 1.4.3 contrast, 2.2.1 timing adjustable, 3.3.1 error identification, 3.3.3 error suggestion, 4.1.3 status messages)
$source.CONV: apple-skill web convention (not stated by Apple)

note: The HIG Feedback page gives NO numbers: no durations, sizes, counts or colours. Everything below tagged HIG is a rule or a named example from the page; every number is tagged CONV or WCAG.

principle.match: The most effective feedback matches the significance of the information to the way it is delivered.
principle.passive: Status information is often best shown passively, so people can look at it when they need it.
principle.interrupting: A warning about possible data loss should interrupt, so people get a chance to avoid the problem.
kinds: success or failure of an important task or action
warning about an action with negative consequences
opportunity to correct a mistake or problematic situation

status.delivery: passive, integrated next to the item it describes (HIG example: Mail shows the latest update and the unread count in the mailbox toolbar)
status.persistence: stays as long as the state is true

successRoutine.delivery: no separate confirmation; the interface simply reflects the new state (people expect success)

successSignificant.kind: a significant action or task completed (HIG example: a successful Apple Pay transaction)
successSignificant.delivery: a brief, non-blocking confirmation near the action

cannotCarryOut.kind: a command can't be carried out
cannotCarryOut.delivery: tell people it can't be done AND why, at the control or in the place they asked (HIG example: Maps says it can't route from and to the same location)

correction.kind: an opportunity to correct a mistake or problematic situation
correction.delivery: inline, right next to the problem, at the moment it is detected
correction.role: alert (or aria-describedby on the invalid field)

warningDataLoss.kind: an action that can cause data loss that is unexpected AND irreversible
warningDataLoss.delivery: interrupt: an alert that names the consequence and offers the safe choice (HIG: alerts deliver critical, ideally actionable, information)
warningDataLoss.doNotWarn: when the data loss is the expected result of the action (HIG example: the Finder does not warn on every file thrown away)

alerts.cost: Alerts disrupt the current context by design; overuse or unimportant content makes them lose their impact.

webConv.noneOnLoad: no alertdialog/modal is open on first paint without a user action
webConv.neverNativeDialogsForSuccess: window.alert() / confirm() are not used to report routine success

accessibility.rule: Provide feedback through more than one channel so people receive it however they use the device.
accessibility.hig: Colour, text, sound and haptics together: people get it if they silence the device, look away, or use VoiceOver.

webConv.announce: every dynamically shown message is exposed to assistive tech (role=status / role=alert / aria-live / aria-describedby on the field)
webConv.spinnerNeedsName: an indeterminate spinner has an accessible name or a live status text

timing.src: CONV / WCAG 2.2.1 — the HIG gives no durations
timing.transientMessageRule: visible at least max(5000 ms, 60 ms × characters); pause on hover/focus; a way to dismiss
timing.errorsAndWarnings: do not auto-dismiss; they stay until resolved or dismissed by the person
timing.toastQueue: one transient message at a time; the newest replaces or queues, never stacks more than 3

controls.src: HIG (show when a command can't be carried out and why) + CONV
controls.disabledNeedsReason: a disabled primary control has a visible or programmatically associated reason (aria-describedby), or stays enabled and explains on press
controls.requiredBeforeContinue: Next/Continue is available only after required data is provided (HIG Entering data) and the missing item is named

watchOS.avoidIndeterminateProgress: Don't show an indeterminate progress indicator in a watchOS app; an animated indicator implies people must keep watching. Tell people they will be notified when the process completes.
watchOS.webConv: On glanceable, small or background surfaces (widgets, wearables, PWAs, long-running jobs) prefer a determinate progress value or 'we will notify you' over an endless spinner.

wording.src: Writing page (hig/foundations/writing.md) — applies to feedback copy
wording.state: say what happened and what to do next; no blame
